ordered_diagnoses: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of the parotid gland
Paraneoplastic Cushing's syndrome due to other neuroendocrine tumors

s1.syndrome_frame: A middle-aged woman with a parotid gland mass and subsequent development of systemic symptoms including facial swelling, abdominal bloating, easy bruising, and significant weight gain, with a prolonged time course of 18 months
salient_findings: Facial swelling, abdominal bloating, easy bruising, and significant weight gain
Elevated serum cortisol and ACTH levels
key_facts: 52-year-old woman presented with a mass on her left parotid gland
Initial presentation included otalgia without constitutional symptoms
Developed facial swelling, abdominal bloating, easy bruising, and 30-lb weight gain 18 months after initial presentation
Blood pressure elevated from 120/78 mm Hg to 193/113 mm Hg over 18 months
Imaging showed a 2.4-cm parotid mass and a 2.7-cm level IIB lymph node
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy showed features of a salivary gland neoplasm with atypia
Serum cortisol level was 1151 nmol/L, exceeding the normal range
ACTH level was 78.5 pmol/L, exceeding the normal range
Random blood glucose was elevated at 16 mmol/L
Potassium level was low at 3.0 mmol/L
Aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase levels were elevated
24-hour urine cortisol was elevated on two consecutive days
Midnight salivary cortisol was elevated on two consecutive nights
Histological examination showed stage T2N2B disease with lymphovascular and perineural invasion
Immunohistochemical staining was positive for ACTH in 30-40% of invasive tumor cells

raw.rationale: The patient's elevated serum cortisol, ACTH level, and midnight salivary cortisol, along with the presence of a parotid gland mass and positive immunohistochemical staining for ACTH in tumor cells, support the diagnosis of an ectopic ACTH-producing tumor.

rejected.label: Cushing's syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient exhibits symptoms of Cushing's syndrome, this is a broader condition that can result from various causes, including ectopic ACTH production, but it does not specifically identify the underlying cause.

rejected.label: Parotid gland adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The presence of a parotid gland mass and features of a salivary gland neoplasm with atypia do not fully explain the patient's hormonal imbalances and other systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of the parotid gland
rejected.why: Although the tumor has neuroendocrine features, the specific diagnosis of ectopic ACTH-producing tumor better explains the patient's clinical presentation and laboratory findings.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic Cushing's syndrome due to other neuroendocrine tumors
rejected.why: The evidence points to the parotid gland tumor as the source of ACTH production, making this option less likely.
